label: Старший / Младший
description: Старший vs младший: elder/younger contrasts across genders and everyday scenes.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Старший' takes the masculine ending to match 'брат', marking him as the elder sibling. The family phrase introduces the seniority sense.

missions.phrase: Моя младшая сестра ходит в школу.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Младшая' takes the feminine ending to match 'сестра', marking her as the younger sibling. The sentence roots the form in family life.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Младшие' takes the plural ending to match 'классы', the lower grades at school. The phrase shows the rank sense in an everyday setting.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Старшее' takes the neuter ending to match 'поколение', the elder generation. The sentence fixes the neuter form in a clear context.
Strategic focus: Direct masculine contrast. 'Старший' is nominative for 'сын' while 'младшему' is dative standing in for the younger one. The pairing sets both ranks against each other.
Strategic focus: Plural agreement used substantively. 'Старшие' matches 'дети' and means the older children. The sentence shows how the form names the elder ones.
Strategic focus: Comparative form as a question. 'Старше' is the comparative of 'старший' and stays the same for any gender. The question asks which of the two is older.
Strategic focus: Masculine agreement in a title. 'Младший' matches 'сотрудник' and marks a junior rank at work. The phrase shows the seniority sense beyond family.
Strategic focus: Feminine agreement naming the younger child. 'Младшая' matches 'дочь' and marks her as the younger daughter. The sentence keeps the rank in a family scene.

Strategic focus: Plural substantive contrast. Both adjectives stand alone as nouns, 'старшие' as the elders in the nominative and 'младшим' as the younger ones in the dative. The proverb-like line pairs both ranks.
